statement_blocker: The catalog supplies only a broad generating-function method gloss. It does not select ordinary, exponential, multivariate, probability, cycle-index, or Dirichlet generating functions; formal versus analytic semantics; coefficient carrier; indexed sequence or combinatorial class; operation or recurrence; ordered binders; hypotheses; conclusion; or algebraic and convergence boundary cases. Choosing coefficient recovery, Cauchy convolution, recurrence solving, a combinatorial product rule, the exponential formula, or a specialized sequence identity would invent or substitute proposition-changing mathematics.
target_decision: redirect the catalog method label to one corrected, independently reviewed, source-selected truth-valued proposition before ordinary statement or proof execution
domain_and_universes: Open: an accepted source must fix the coefficient carrier and algebraic or topological structure, index type, sequence or combinatorial class, formal-series or analytic-function semantics, variables, evaluation domain, convergence structure, universes, and all typeclass context.
conclusion: Open: the repository does not choose a definition/recovery fact, Cauchy-product identity, recurrence solution, combinatorial construction theorem, exponential formula, coefficient-extraction result, specialized sequence identity, or analytic/asymptotic conclusion.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded before a proposition is selected; the statement phase must resolve every coefficient, index, algebraic, empty/zero, support, composition, convergence, rearrangement, and boundary case listed in scope-map.md.

the labeled exponential formula for an explicitly defined combinatorial class

degenerate_cases_to_resolve: empty sequence or class, zero and singleton indices, and finite versus infinite support
zero divisors, noncommutative coefficients, and natural versus signed or field-valued counts
missing or negative indices and recurrence initial-condition range
empty sums and products, nonunit denominators, and composition at nonzero constant term
formal coefficientwise equality versus equality after analytic evaluation
open disk, radius boundary, divergence, and zero-radius series
interchange or rearrangement of infinite sums, products, derivatives, and limits
